findings: New raw lines 5-18 and old raw lines 4-17 retain the Checkout Sessions discount purpose and separate Payment Intents route: calculate the discounted amount server-side and create or update the PaymentIntent. This is not a coupon parameter on a PaymentIntent.

New raw lines 20-66 and old raw lines 19-81 retain coupon identity and behavior: a Coupon defines percent/fixed amount and product/redemption/expiry limits; a Checkout Session's discounts array accepts a coupon ID, with at most one coupon or promotion code. Deleting a Coupon prevents future applications, not retroactive reversal.

New raw lines 68-106 and old raw lines 83-133 retain promotion codes as customer-facing aliases to an existing Coupon. Code uniqueness applies across active codes, with customer-restricted reuse distinguished from general-use codes. Server-created Sessions enable allow_promotion_codes, then browser Checkout Elements actions apply/remove an entered code.

The substantive documented sample change is React's import/useCheckout() in old raw lines 172-191 to import/useCheckoutElements() in new raw lines 140-161; both reference the same @stripe/react-stripe-js/checkout entrypoint and checkoutState.checkout action methods. answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/discounts, new raw lines 5-106 and 140-227 describe Checkout Sessions discounts: a server applies a Coupon ID through discounts or enables allow_promotion_codes so a customer can enter a Promotion Code mapped to a Coupon. The Elements client applies or removes the code; a Session supports at most one coupon or promotion code. Coupons and codes have product, customer, redemption, expiry, first-time and minimum-amount limits, while Payment Intents require server-side discounted amount calculation. Compared with old raw lines 4-133 and 172-256, source-stripe-checkout-add-discounts.md correctly summarizes the core flow, but has only April provenance and no dated React hook distinction. Discount application does not establish payment success.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/discounts, the substantive sample delta is old raw lines 176-178 importing and calling useCheckout() versus new raw lines 144-147 using useCheckoutElements() from the same React checkout entrypoint. source-stripe-checkout-add-discounts.md should add November provenance and label both dated examples, while preserving its coupon, promotion-code and client-action baseline. The Node-to-curl request examples in old raw lines 23-59 and 108-131 versus new raw lines 24-44 and 93-104 carry the same material parameters; formatting and link changes are presentational. The new example does not prove useCheckout removal, an SDK compatibility floor, payment completion, or a new PaymentIntent coupon API; the separate versioned checkout concept retains the alias qualification.
